correctness.rationale: With A=(I+L)^{-1} and added edge bbᵀ, Sherman–Morrison gives mean-zero transform T=I−(Ab)bᵀ/(1+r). The nontrivial singular-square eigenvalues have trace 2(1+r+τ)/(1+r)² and product 1/(1+r)², r=bᵀAb, τ=bᵀA²b≤r. Evaluate its quadratic q(3/2)=((1−3r)²/4+3(r−τ))/(1+r)²≥0 and λ−<1 to get λ+≤3/2. Equality would force r=τ=1/3 but then Ab=b and r=2, impossible; 2 disjoint weighted K6 give r,τ→1/3, sharp. Independent 161 randomly weighted graph eigenvalue comparisons and exact path witness factor 1647/1600 verified; universal proof is analytic.
